When Awareness Isn’t Enough

Data can show us what we are doing. Change often begins only when we understand why we are doing it.

Through My Quiet LensNovember 6, 20252 min read
#Digitalwellbeing#Behaviour#Reflection

I used to think I had a healthy relationship with my phone. A few scrolls between meetings, maybe a video before bed, nothing major.

Then, in my Happiness class, we were asked to track how we spend our time. I thought it’d be quick, a few numbers, maybe a chart.

Instead, it showed me something uncomfortable: Every 30 minutes or so, I was spending about five minutes scrolling. By day’s end, nearly two hours gone .

Apple’s Screen Time confirmed it. But the data didn’t change my habits. Awareness alone wasn’t enough.

That’s when I decided to dig deeper.

Apple’s reports looked neat, but vague. Four hours on my phone… doing what exactly? Learning or doom-scrolling?

I set daily limits. Then hit “Ignore for today” , every single day.

One day scroll too many. That’s when I realized. I didn’t lack data. I lacked meaning.

So, each time I picked up my phone, I wrote why , scrolling, learning, listening, or just passing time.

Within days, patterns appeared. I wasn’t tracking time anymore, I was tracking intent. And that shift changed everything.

👉 Awareness tells you what you’re doing.

👉 Meaning tells you why you’re doing it. That’s when real change begins.

Now, when I reach for my phone, I pause, not to judge, but to ask, why now? That small question keeps me honest.

If Apple ever asked for feedback, I’d tell them: Don’t just show hours. Show purpose. Help people reflect on how that time feels.

Because data informs. But meaning transforms.
